name: SIA Project 25 26
description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: [https://iris.sad.ve.it/](https://iris.sad.ve.it/?utm_source=gemini). The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source software to all Italian public administrations through the portal [https://developers.italia.it/](https://developers.italia.it/?utm_source=gemini).

A. REPORTS
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin (which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its file path on the server). The possible problem categories are:
• Waterworks – Drinking water
• Architectural Barriers
• Sewerage
• Public Lighting
• Waste
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights
• Roads and Urban Furniture
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds
• Other
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section).
If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), two cases are possible:

* Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved.
Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company (bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.
* Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.

C. CITIZEN UPDATES
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo).
Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description.
Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

highLevelGoals: Citizens aim to effectively report various urban inconveniences and malfunctions to the public administration, providing necessary details and evidence.
Citizens want to be informed about the progress and status changes of their submitted reports, fostering trust and transparency.
Citizens desire to view and track the status of other public reports, understanding the overall urban environment issues and their resolution.
Citizens seek to communicate with municipal operators regarding their reports to provide further information or receive clarifications.
Non-registered users aim to view public reports and statistics to stay informed about urban inconveniences and the municipality's efforts.
Organization Office Staff aims to perform a preliminary review of citizen reports to determine their validity and assign them appropriate statuses (accepted/rejected).
Organization Office Staff seeks to provide mandatory written explanations for rejected reports to maintain transparency and citizen trust.
Technical Office Staff aims to effectively manage approved reports by assigning them to the correct technical offices or external companies based on problem categories.
Technical Office Staff seeks to accurately track and update the status of reports throughout their lifecycle, from 'In Progress' to 'Resolved'.
Technical Office Staff aims to facilitate communication and information exchange with external maintenance personnel to ensure timely resolution of issues.
External Maintenance Personnel aims to receive and access reports assigned to them by the Technical Office for intervention.
External Maintenance Personnel seeks to update the status of reports to reflect the progress of their work, such as 'In Progress' or 'Resolved'.
External Maintenance Personnel aims to exchange information and comments with the Technical Office Staff regarding specific reports.
Municipal Administrator aims to configure various system settings, such as automatic report assignment rules, to optimize operational efficiency.
Municipal Administrator seeks to access both public and private statistics, including charts and tables, to gain insights into system performance and urban issues.

baselineCritiques.actors: The identified actors are comprehensive and accurately reflect the roles described in the system. "Citizen" covers the primary users who register and submit reports. "Non-Registered User" correctly identifies the audience for public statistics and map views. "Organization Office Staff" and "Technical Office Staff" appropriately distinguish the internal administrative roles involved in reviewing and managing reports. "External Maintenance Personnel" captures the third-party entities that receive assigned tasks. "Municipal Administrator" covers the high-level configuration and private statistics access. There are no obvious omissions or contradictions.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The high-level goals are comprehensive, accurately reflecting the functional requirements for all defined actors (Citizens, Non-Registered Users, Staff, External Personnel, and Administrators). They correctly capture the core workflows: reporting, reviewing, assigning, maintaining, and statistical analysis. There are no contradictions with the description, and no major functional omissions are evident. The goals are appropriately abstract (high-level) and functional in nature.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are comprehensive, well-structured, and accurately reflect the functional requirements derived from the high-level goals and software description. They correctly map to specific actor actions (e.g., selecting a location, assigning reports, configuring rules) and cover all major workflows (registration, reporting, review, assignment, resolution, statistics). There are no obvious contradictions or major omissions regarding the core functionality described. The distinction between public and private statistics is handled correctly. The goals are appropriately granular for a low-level specification.

hlg_a3ebb05890d39619_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Citizen to create and submit a comprehensive urban inconvenience report by selecting a predefined category, providing a detailed textual description, specifying the exact geographical location, and uploading visual evidence (image or video) to the public administration.
hlg_a3ebb05890d39619_001.rationale: This High-Level Goal reconstructs the complete aggregate scope by integrating all capabilities from the Low-Level Goals. llg_001 contributes the capability for the Citizen to select a predefined category for the urban inconvenience. llg_002 adds the capability for the Citizen to provide a detailed textual description of the inconvenience. llg_003 includes the capability for the Citizen to specify the exact geographical location of the inconvenience. llg_004 introduces the capability for the Citizen to upload an image or video file as visual evidence. Finally, llg_005 completes the process by contributing the capability for the Citizen to finalize and submit the complete report to the public administration.

hlg_9ff35dc9d04a67ca_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Citizen receives automated notifications regarding status changes for their submitted reports, and can access and view the most recent status, as well as a chronological log of all status changes, for any specific report they have submitted.
hlg_9ff35dc9d04a67ca_001.rationale: llg_001 contributes the capability for the Citizen to receive automated notifications when the status of one of their submitted reports changes. llg_002 adds the capability for the Citizen to access and view the most recent status of a specific report they have submitted. llg_003 further adds the capability for the Citizen to view a chronological log of all status changes for a specific report they have submitted. All distinct capabilities are preserved and combined into a single comprehensive goal.
source_low_level_goal_ids: View current status of submitted report
Access status change history for submitted report

hlg_42b1e389973b6476_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Citizens to discover publicly available reports of urban inconveniences by navigating an interactive map, search for specific reports using filters or keywords/location criteria, view their full details, and subscribe to notifications for status changes or comments on specific reports.
hlg_42b1e389973b6476_001.rationale: The reconstructed High-Level Goal aggregates all distinct functional capabilities from the Low-Level Goals. llg_001 contributes the capability for a Citizen to discover reports by navigating an interactive map. llg_002 adds the ability for a Citizen to apply filters to narrow down displayed reports. llg_003 provides the functionality for a Citizen to search for specific reports using keywords or location criteria. llg_004 enables a Citizen to open and view the full details of a specific report. llg_005 introduces the capability for a Citizen to opt to receive notifications for status changes or comments on a specific report, which is summarized as 'subscribe to notifications'.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Browse public reports on interactive map
Select public report to view details
Subscribe to updates for public report

hlg_9ff35dc9d04a67ca_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Receive updates on report status' is supported by Section C (Citizen Updates), which mandates notifications for state changes and allows citizens to view report details. The material outcome set of the HLG is {receive status change notifications, view report status}. The reconstructed HLG' includes {receive status change notifications, view current status, access status change history}. The LLG 'Access status change history' is not explicitly supported by the documentation, which only mentions receiving notifications at every state change and viewing the report page (which displays the current status). While the HLG is valid, the reconstruction adds an unsupported outcome (history log) and the HLG description is slightly broader than the strict 'updates' (notifications) if 'view status' is considered a separate passive capability. However, 'viewing' the report is part of the citizen's interaction. The primary issue is that the reconstruction includes an unsupported LLG (history), making the aggregate HLG' broader than the documented HLG. The HLG itself is valid but could be more precise to exclude the implied 'history' if that is not a feature. Given the HLG is supported and the reconstruction is a superset (adding unsupported history), the relationship is PARTIAL_OVERLAP (HLG' adds an outcome not in HLG). The HLG is valid, so KEEP. Voting result 2/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The parent HLG 'Receive updates on report status' is grounded in Section C, which states citizens receive notifications at every state change and can view report details. llg_001 is supported by 'citizen receives a notification on the platform'. llg_002 is supported by the ability to view report details (title/description) which inherently includes status visibility in the context of tracking progress. However, llg_003 ('chronological log of all status changes') is not explicitly documented. Section C mentions receiving notifications for changes and viewing current status/details, but does not specify a persistent, viewable historical log of all past status transitions for a specific report. While notifications are sent, the documentation does not entail that the citizen can access a consolidated history view of these changes. Therefore, llg_003 is an unsupported addition.

hlg_42b1e389973b6476_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'View and follow public reports' is supported by Section C, which allows citizens to view public reports on a map/table and follow other citizens' open reports to receive notifications. The material outcomes of the HLG are {view public reports, follow/track public reports}. The reconstructed HLG' aggregates the LLGs into {navigate map, filter, search, view details, subscribe to notifications}. HLG' entails the HLG outcomes (viewing is covered by navigate/view details; following is covered by subscribe). However, HLG' adds specific interaction mechanisms (filter, search) that are not explicitly enumerated as distinct outcomes in the HLG description, though they are implied by 'view'. More critically, the HLG description 'understanding the overall urban environment issues' is a vague outcome not strictly entailed by the specific LLGs which focus on individual report discovery and tracking. The LLGs are valid and supported by the documentation (Section C mentions map, table, filtering, sorting, and following). The parent is valid but the reconstruction is a more detailed operationalization. The relationship is PARTIAL_OVERLAP because the reconstruction adds specific capabilities (filter/search) not explicitly named in the parent's high-level description, and the parent's 'understanding' clause is not fully captured by the LLGs. The parent is supported, so it should be kept, and the LLGs need evaluation to ensure they align with the 'follow' aspect (which is supported by 'receive notifications' in LLG 005). Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The decomposition is incomplete and contains unsupported capabilities. The parent HLG 'View and follow public reports' explicitly requires the ability to 'follow' reports, which the documentation defines as receiving notifications for status changes on other citizens' reports. While llg_005 mentions subscribing to updates, it incorrectly includes 'comments' in the notification scope; the documentation states that comments exchanged between technical staff and external maintainers are not visible to citizens, and citizens only receive notifications for state changes or messages from operators, not comments. Furthermore, the documentation explicitly supports viewing reports in a 'summary table' in addition to the map, which is missing from the LLGs. llg_003 (Search) is also unsupported as the documentation only mentions filtering and sorting, not keyword search.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: [https://iris.sad.ve.it/](https://iris.sad.ve.it/?utm_source=gemini). The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source software to all Italian public administrations through the portal [https://developers.italia.it/](https://developers.italia.it/?utm_source=gemini).

A. REPORTS
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin (which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its file path on the server). The possible problem categories are:
• Waterworks – Drinking water
• Architectural Barriers
• Sewerage
• Public Lighting
• Waste
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights
• Roads and Urban Furniture
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds
• Other
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section).
If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), two cases are possible:

* Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved.
Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company (bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.
* Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.

C. CITIZEN UPDATES
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo).
Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description.
Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section).
If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), two cases are possible:

* Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved.
Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company (bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.
* Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.

C. CITIZEN UPDATES
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo).
Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description.
Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

hlg_9ff35dc9d04a67ca_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Receive updates on report status' expresses the citizen's outcome of being informed about report progress. The documentation (Section C) supports this via automated notifications, platform messages, and visibility of status changes. The reconstruction HLG' aggregates the LLGs: {receive automated notifications, view current status, view status history}. Comparing the sets: HLG' entails HLG (notifications are a form of update). However, HLG does not explicitly entail the specific capabilities of 'viewing current status' or 'viewing status history' as distinct functional outcomes separate from passive notification receipt. While these are related, the reconstruction introduces specific on-demand viewing capabilities not explicitly bounded in the original HLG description, which focuses on 'being informed' (passive). More critically, the original HLG is a valid, supported parent. The reconstruction is a lossless aggregate of the children. The relationship is PARTIAL_OVERLAP because the reconstruction adds specific viewing mechanisms (current status, history log) that are not explicitly stated in the original HLG's description, although they are implied by 'updates'. However, looking closer at the documentation, 'updates' includes notifications and messages. The LLGs include 'View current status' and 'Access status change history'. These are distinct from 'receiving notifications'. The original HLG is broad enough to cover them, but the reconstruction is more specific. Is it EQUIVALENT? HLG' entails HLG. Does HLG entail HLG'? 'Receive updates' is vague. It doesn't strictly entail 'viewing history logs'. Therefore, it is PARTIAL_OVERLAP. The parent is valid and supported. The LLGs need evaluation to ensure they don't exceed the parent's scope or miss essential parts. Since the parent is valid, we KEEP it and require LLG evaluation to check if the specific LLGs (like viewing history) are correctly scoped under this HLG or if they belong elsewhere (e.g., if 'View public reports' covers history, but this is for *own* reports). The sibling 'View and follow public reports' is for *other* citizens' reports. This HLG is for *own* reports. Thus, no redundancy. The parent is valid. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The LLGs are not fully supported by the documentation. llg_001 is supported by Section C, which states citizens receive notifications on the platform at every state change. However, llg_002 and llg_003 are unsupported. The documentation specifies that accepted reports appear on a map and in a summary table where the 'status' is displayed, but it does not document a specific feature for a citizen to view a 'chronological log of all status changes' (llg_003) or a dedicated view for the 'most recent status' distinct from the public list (llg_002). While the public list shows status, the specific capability of accessing a historical log of changes for one's own report is not explicitly entailed; the documentation only guarantees notifications of changes, not a persistent historical log viewable on demand. Therefore, llg_002 and llg_003 represent undocumented capabilities or misinterpretations of the public list functionality.

hlg_42b1e389973b6476_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'View and follow public reports' is supported by Section C, which allows citizens to view public reports on maps/tables and follow other citizens' reports. The HLG outcome set is {view, follow}. The reconstruction HLG' outcome set is {discover, filter, search, view details, subscribe}. HLG' entails 'view' (via view details) and 'follow' (via subscribe), but adds 'discover', 'filter', and 'search' which are specific interaction mechanisms not explicitly enumerated as distinct high-level outcomes in the original HLG description, though they are part of the 'view' capability in the documentation. However, the original HLG description 'view and track the status' is broader than just 'view details'; it implies monitoring. The reconstruction is a lossless aggregate of the LLGs provided. The relationship is PARTIAL_OVERLAP because the reconstruction introduces specific granular actions (filter, search) that expand the scope of the original high-level goal's explicit wording, although they are functionally subordinate to 'view'. The original HLG is valid and supported. The LLGs need evaluation to ensure they don't overstep the 'public' scope or include private report features. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The decomposition is incomplete and contains unsupported capabilities. The documentation explicitly states that accepted reports appear in a 'summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date.' The current LLGs cover filtering (llg_002) but omit the explicit capability to 'sort' reports, which is a distinct functional requirement. Additionally, llg_003 ('Search for public reports') is unsupported; the documentation only mentions filtering and sorting, not keyword or location-based search. replacement_request.generation_project_description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: [https://iris.sad.ve.it/](https://iris.sad.ve.it/?utm_source=gemini). The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source software to all Italian public administrations through the portal [https://developers.italia.it/](https://developers.italia.it/?utm_source=gemini).

A. REPORTS
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin (which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its file path on the server). The possible problem categories are:
• Waterworks – Drinking water
• Architectural Barriers
• Sewerage
• Public Lighting
• Waste
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights
• Roads and Urban Furniture
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds
• Other
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section).
If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), two cases are possible:

* Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved.
Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company (bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.
* Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.

C. CITIZEN UPDATES
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo).
Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description.
Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

hlg_a3ebb05890d39619_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Report urban inconveniences' is fully supported by the documentation (Section A), which details the citizen's ability to submit reports with specific fields (title, description, category, location, photos) and anonymity options. The material outcome set of the HLG is {report urban inconveniences, provide details, provide evidence}. The reconstructed HLG' explicitly enumerates {select category, provide description, specify location, upload evidence, submit report}. These sets are semantically equivalent: the reconstruction aggregates the specific LLGs into the same functional intention as the parent without adding unsupported outcomes (e.g., it does not claim video support which is not in the docs, though the LLG mentions it, the HLG' text is a faithful aggregate of the provided LLGs which are the source for this comparison). The actor (Citizen) and scope (reporting) match perfectly. No sibling branch covers this specific reporting capability; they cover updates, viewing public reports, and interaction. Therefore, the parent is valid and the reconstruction is equivalent.

hlg_9ff35dc9d04a67ca_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Receive updates on report status' is supported by Section C (Citizen Updates), which mandates notifications for state changes and allows citizens to view report details. The material outcome set of the HLG is {receive status change notifications, view report status}. The reconstructed HLG' outcome set is {receive automated notifications, view current status, view status change history}. HLG' entails HLG (notifications and status viewing are covered). However, HLG' adds 'view status change history' (chronological log), which is not explicitly stated as a distinct capability in the original HLG description, although it is a plausible interpretation of 'updates'. More critically, the original HLG description focuses on 'progress and status changes', which aligns with the notifications and current status. The addition of 'history' in HLG' makes it broader than the original HLG's explicit scope, or the original HLG is slightly under-specified if history is considered part of 'updates'. Given the strict equivalence requirement, HLG' is not strictly equivalent because it explicitly includes 'chronological log' which is not in the HLG text. However, looking at the LLGs, llg_003 is 'Access status change history'. If the HLG is meant to cover all citizen update mechanisms, it should include history. The HLG description 'informed about the progress and status changes' is arguably sufficient to cover history, but the reconstruction is more specific. Let's look at the sibling 'View and follow public reports'. That is for *other* reports. This HLG is for *own* reports. The HLG is valid. The reconstruction adds specificity. Is it PARTIAL_OVERLAP? HLG' covers HLG. Does HLG cover HLG'? 'Receive updates' can be interpreted to include history. But strict entailment: Does 'Receive updates' entail 'View chronological log'? Not necessarily. Does 'View chronological log' entail 'Receive updates'? No, it's a specific view. Therefore, they are not equivalent. HLG' is a superset or different formulation. Since HLG' adds 'history' which is a distinct LLG, and the HLG doesn't explicitly mention history, it's PARTIAL_OVERLAP (HLG' adds an outcome). Wait, if HLG' adds an outcome, it's PARTIAL_OVERLAP. The parent is valid (supported by docs). So KEEP with requires_llg_evaluation=true. Voting result 2/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. llg_001 is explicitly supported by Section C ('at every state change, the citizen receives a notification'). llg_002 is supported by the requirement for citizens to be informed about progress and the visibility of reports on the portal. However, llg_003 ('chronological log of all status changes') is not explicitly documented. Section C mentions notifications for changes and viewing current status, but does not mandate a persistent, viewable history log for the citizen. While the system tracks states, the specific capability of viewing a full chronological log is an inferred feature not entailed by the text, which focuses on notifications and current state visibility. Therefore, llg_003 is unsupported.

hlg_9ff35dc9d04a67ca_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Receive updates on report status' is supported by Section C (Citizen Updates), which mandates notifications for state changes and allows citizens to view report details. The material outcome set of the HLG is {receive status change notifications, view report status}. The reconstructed HLG' explicitly entails {receive system-sent notifications when status changes, retrieve and display most recent status}. Bidirectional entailment holds: HLG' covers the push (notification) and pull (viewing) mechanisms described in the documentation, and the original HLG's intent to be 'informed about progress and status changes' is fully captured by these two mechanisms. No essential outcomes are missing or added. The actor (Citizen) and scope (own reports) match the documentation. The LLGs align with the reconstruction. Therefore, the relationship is EQUIVALENT and the parent is valid.

The original HLG 'View and follow public reports' is fully supported by Section C of the documentation, which states that citizens can view public reports on a map and table, and follow other citizens' open reports to receive notifications. The material outcome set of the HLG is {view public reports, follow public reports}. The reconstructed HLG' aggregates the LLGs into {view on map, filter, select details, follow, view in table, sort}. hlg_614a9646fc92d22e_001.rationale: Voting result 2/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Manage and assign approved reports' is supported by the documentation, which states that after approval, reports are assigned to the technical office responsible based on the problem category. The material outcome set of the HLG is {assign to internal office, assign to external company}. The reconstruction HLG' includes {retrieve list, view details, assign to internal office, assign to external company, categorize by problem type}. HLG' entails the HLG outcomes (assignment), but the HLG does not entail the retrieval, viewing, or categorization outcomes present in HLG'. Thus, the relationship is PARTIAL_OVERLAP. The parent is valid but narrow; the LLGs include auxiliary capabilities (retrieval, viewing, categorization) that are not explicitly in the parent's description. The parent should be kept, and the LLGs require evaluation to ensure they align with the documented scope. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The documentation (Section D) supports public statistics (counts, trends) and private statistics (charts, tables) for administrators. However, the original HLG does not explicitly mention 'generating custom reports' or 'exporting data'. The reconstructed HLG' includes these capabilities based on the LLGs (llg_003, llg_004). Since the documentation does not explicitly support 'generating custom reports' or 'exporting data' as distinct functional outcomes for the administrator (it only mentions viewing charts/tables), the LLGs llg_003 and llg_004 are likely unsupported or over-specified. The relationship is PARTIAL_OVERLAP because HLG' adds outcomes (custom reports, export) not in the original HLG or documentation. replacement_request.generation_project_description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: [https://iris.sad.ve.it/](https://iris.sad.ve.it/?utm_source=gemini). The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source software to all Italian public administrations through the portal [https://developers.italia.it/](https://developers.italia.it/?utm_source=gemini).

A. REPORTS
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin (which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its file path on the server). The possible problem categories are:
• Waterworks – Drinking water
• Architectural Barriers
• Sewerage
• Public Lighting
• Waste
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights
• Roads and Urban Furniture
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds
• Other
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section).
If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), two cases are possible:

* Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved.
Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company (bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.
* Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.

C. CITIZEN UPDATES
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo).
Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description.
Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo).
Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description.
Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

hlg_a3ebb05890d39619_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. hlg_9ff35dc9d04a67ca_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Receive updates on report status' is supported by Section C, which mandates that citizens receive notifications on the platform and via email at every state change. The material outcome set of the HLG is {receive status change notifications}. The reconstructed HLG' includes {receive status change notifications, retrieve/display current status}. While the notification outcome is shared, HLG' adds the capability to actively retrieve and display status, which is not explicitly entailed by the original HLG's description of being 'informed' (which primarily implies the push mechanism described in the documentation). Therefore, the relationship is PARTIAL_OVERLAP. The original HLG is valid and supported, so it should be kept, and the LLGs require evaluation to ensure they align with the documented scope. Voting result 2/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The decomposition is incomplete. Section C of the documentation explicitly states that 'municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply.' This capability is a distinct mechanism for receiving updates and interacting with the administration regarding report status, separate from the automatic status change notifications (llg_001) and the passive retrieval of status (llg_002). The current LLGs omit this essential communication channel. Furthermore, while llg_002 covers retrieving status, the documentation emphasizes that citizens can 'follow' their reports, which implies a continuous tracking capability that is partially addressed by llg_001 but the specific ability to view the detailed history or current state via the portal is a core part of 'receiving updates' as described in the 'Citizen Updates' section. However, the most critical omission is the messaging capability which is explicitly documented as a way citizens receive updates/information from operators. Therefore, the decomposition fails to cover all essential capabilities defined in the parent HLG and documentation.

hlg_a3ebb05890d39619_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Citizen creates and submits a comprehensive report of an urban inconvenience by selecting a predefined category, providing a detailed textual description, specifying the exact geographical location (potentially using a map interface or address input), and uploading an image or video file as visual evidence, before finalizing and submitting the complete report to the public administration.
hlg_a3ebb05890d39619_001.rationale: The reconstructed high-level goal describes the comprehensive process by which a Citizen creates and submits a report of an urban inconvenience. llg_001 contributes the capability for the Citizen to select a predefined category for the inconvenience. llg_002 adds the capability for the Citizen to provide a detailed textual description of the inconvenience. llg_003 includes the capability for the Citizen to specify the exact geographical location, explicitly mentioning the potential use of a map interface or address input. llg_004 introduces the capability for the Citizen to upload an image or video file as visual evidence. Finally, llg_005 completes the process by adding the capability for the Citizen to finalize and submit the complete report to the public administration.

hlg_9ff35dc9d04a67ca_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable citizens to be informed about the status of their submitted reports by receiving system-sent notifications when the report status changes and by allowing them to retrieve and display the most recent status of a specific submitted report.
hlg_9ff35dc9d04a67ca_001.rationale: The reconstructed high-level goal combines the distinct capabilities from both low-level goals. llg_001 contributes the capability for the system to proactively send notifications to the citizen when the status of their submitted report changes. llg_002 contributes the capability for the citizen to actively retrieve and display the most recent status of a specific report they have submitted. Both goals collectively aim to keep the citizen informed about the status of their submitted reports, through both push (notification) and pull (retrieval/display) mechanisms.
source_low_level_goal_ids: View current status of submitted report

hlg_42b1e389973b6476_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: The system shall enable a Citizen to view public reports, presented on an interactive map interface or in a tabular list with summary information, and to apply filters, sort, select for detailed viewing, and mark reports to receive status updates.
hlg_42b1e389973b6476_001.rationale: This High-Level Goal is a lossless reconstruction of the provided Low-Level Goals. llg_001 contributes the capability for a Citizen to view public reports on an interactive map interface. llg_002 adds the functionality for a Citizen to apply filters to public reports based on various criteria. llg_003 introduces the ability for a Citizen to select a specific public report to view its detailed information. llg_004 includes the distinct capability for a Citizen to mark a public report to receive updates on its status changes. llg_005 specifies the ability for a Citizen to view public reports in a tabular list format, showing key summary information. llg_006 adds the functionality for a Citizen to sort the displayed public reports based on various attributes.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Browse public reports on interactive map
Select public report to view details
View public reports in summary table

hlg_0a9173cad26c8343_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Citizen engages in two-way message exchange with a municipal operator concerning submitted reports and inquiries, specifically by composing and sending messages about submitted reports, receiving messages in response to reports or inquiries, and accessing and reviewing the complete message exchange history related to specific reports.
hlg_0a9173cad26c8343_001.rationale: The reconstructed high-level goal integrates all distinct functional capabilities from the low-level goals. llg_001 introduces the ability for a Citizen to initiate communication by composing and sending messages to a municipal operator concerning a specific report they submitted. llg_002 introduces the ability for a Citizen to receive messages from a municipal operator, expanding the scope of communication to include responses to both reports and general inquiries. llg_003 introduces the ability for a Citizen to access and review the entire historical record of message exchanges pertaining to a specific report.

The original HLG 'Receive updates on report status' captures the intent of being informed about progress and status changes. The reconstruction HLG' aggregates the LLGs: 'Receive report status change notification' (push) and 'View current status of submitted report' (pull). Both outcomes are explicitly supported by the documentation: 'at every state change, the citizen receives a notification' and the ability to view report details/status. The material outcome set of the HLG is {be informed of status changes/progress}. The material outcome set of HLG' is {receive status change notification, view current status}. HLG' entails HLG because both mechanisms serve the goal of being informed. There is no actor mismatch (Citizen). There is no unsupported content. The sibling 'View and follow public reports' concerns *other* citizens' reports, whereas this HLG concerns *their own* reports, so it is not redundant. The reconstruction is a faithful, lossless aggregate of the children which aligns with the parent's intent.

hlg_0a9173cad26c8343_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Interact with public administration' is supported by Section C, which allows citizens to receive messages from operators and reply. The material outcome set of the HLG is {communicate, provide information, receive clarifications}. The reconstructed HLG' outcome set is {send message, receive message, view history}. HLG' entails the core communication loop (send/receive) but adds 'view history' which is not explicitly stated in the HLG description, and the HLG's 'provide information' is a subset of 'send message'. While the intent is aligned, the HLG description is vague ('interact') compared to the specific messaging capabilities in the documentation and LLGs. The LLGs correctly decompose the messaging functionality. The relationship is PARTIAL_OVERLAP because the reconstruction is more specific and includes history viewing, which the parent implies but does not explicitly delimit as a distinct outcome. The parent is valid but could be more precise; however, it is not materially wrong. It is not redundant with siblings (updates vs messaging). Voting result 2/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The decomposition is incomplete. The parent HLG 'Interact with public administration' and the project description (Section C) explicitly state that citizens can 'reply' to messages sent by municipal operators. While llg_001 covers sending messages regarding reports, it does not explicitly cover the act of replying to an incoming message, which is a distinct interaction flow initiated by the operator. Furthermore, llg_002 describes receiving messages, but the ability to actively respond (reply) is a core part of the 'two-way' communication described in the HLG description ('provide further information or receive clarifications'). The current LLGs treat sending and receiving as separate, static actions, missing the interactive 'reply' capability which is explicitly documented. Additionally, llg_003 (viewing history) is supported, but the omission of the explicit 'reply' action creates a gap in the documented interaction loop. Therefore, the essential capability of replying to operator messages is missing.

hlg_5e5af4df50bf374f_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The documentation mandates that the Organization Office provides a written explanation when rejecting a report. The original HLG outcomes are {provide explanation}, while the reconstruction HLG' outcomes are {type, save, send explanation}. HLG' entails HLG (sending implies providing), but HLG does not strictly entail the specific workflow steps of typing and saving, making the relationship PARTIAL_OVERLAP. However, the original HLG is valid, supported, and correctly scoped to the actor's responsibility. The sibling branch covers the review decision (accept/reject), not the explanation provision, so no redundancy exists. The parent is kept for LLG evaluation. Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The parent HLG requires Organization Office Staff to provide mandatory written explanations for rejected reports. The documentation explicitly states that a written explanation is mandatory in case of rejection. llg_001 covers the creation/entry of this explanation ('types in a required explanation'), and llg_002 covers the finalization/submission ('saves and sends'). These two LLGs accurately decompose the single documented capability of providing the explanation into logical steps (input and submission) without introducing unsupported actions (like notifications or status changes, which are handled elsewhere or implied by the submission). There are no missing essential capabilities for this specific HLG, as the core requirement is the provision of the text itself. The decomposition is precise and supported by the text.

hlg_0a9173cad26c8343_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Citizens to exchange messages with municipal operators concerning specific reports, encompassing the sending of initial messages, provision of further information, sending of direct responses to received messages, reception of messages or clarifications, and the retrieval and display of the complete history of exchanged messages.
hlg_0a9173cad26c8343_001.rationale: llg_001 contributes the capability for the Citizen to initiate communication with a municipal operator by sending an initial message or to provide updates by sending further information regarding a report. llg_002 adds the capability for the Citizen to receive communication, specifically messages or clarifications, from a municipal operator regarding their submitted reports. llg_003 introduces the capability for the Citizen to access and review past interactions by retrieving and displaying the complete history of messages exchanged with municipal operators for a specific report. llg_004 specifies the capability for the Citizen to send a message in direct response to a specific message received from a municipal operator, providing clarifications or additional details.

Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The documentation (Section C) supports the Citizen's ability to exchange messages with municipal operators regarding their reports, including sending messages, receiving messages, and replying. The original HLG 'Interact with public administration' describes this communication intent. The reconstructed HLG' explicitly enumerates the outcomes: sending initial messages, providing further information, sending direct responses, receiving messages/clarifications, and retrieving conversation history. The material outcome sets are semantically equivalent: both cover the bidirectional exchange of information and the review of that history. The original HLG is supported by the documentation and correctly scoped to the Citizen actor. The reconstruction accurately aggregates the LLGs without adding unsupported capabilities or omitting essential ones. No sibling HLG covers this specific communication capability (other branches cover reporting, status updates, and viewing public reports).
